about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Baked Cheese Crisps
recipes.summary: Lacy, crunchy oven-baked cheese crisps with a pinch of smoked paprika.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper.
Mix the cheese, paprika and pepper, then drop heaped tablespoons 4cm apart on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 8 minutes, until the edges are deep golden and the centres have stopped bubbling. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes to crisp.
notes: Snack. Per serving: about 4 crisps. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container. Check the label to confirm the cheese is made with vegetarian rennet.

recipes.title: Rye Seed Crispbread
recipes.summary: Thin, crunchy Scandinavian-style rye crispbread with sesame and sunflower seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flours, seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and water to form a firm dough.
Divide into 2, roll each piece between 2 sheets of baking paper to 3mm thick and prick all over with a fork. Slide onto the trays and cut into 12 rectangles.
Bake for 25 minutes, swapping trays halfway, until crisp and golden at the edges. Cool on a rack; they crisp further as they cool.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 pieces of crispbread. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Seeded Oat Crackers
recipes.summary: Nutty, sturdy crackers loaded with oats, pumpkin and sunflower seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and water to a firm dough.
Roll out between 2 sheets of baking paper to 3mm thick, slide onto a tray and cut into 24 squares.
Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp, turning the tray halfway. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackers. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Rosemary Olive Crackers
recipes.summary: Thin olive oil crackers flecked with rosemary and chopped black olives.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flour, salt, rosemary and olives, then stir in the oil and water to a smooth dough.
Roll out between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2mm thick and cut into 24 rectangles with a knife.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackers. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Scottish Oatcakes
recipes.summary: Plain, crumbly oatcakes baked until crisp, good with cheese or hummus.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Blitz the oats in a food processor until coarse.
Mix the oats, salt and butter, then stir in the hot water to make a firm dough. Roll out to 5mm thick on a floured bench and cut into 24 rounds.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until firm and golden at the edges. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 oatcakes. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container. Use certified gluten-free oats if needed.

recipes.title: Lavash Sesame Crackers
recipes.summary: Paper-thin Middle Eastern flatbread crackers snapped into shards.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flour, salt, oil and water into a smooth dough and knead for 2 minutes.
Divide into 4, roll each piece as thinly as you can, brush with a little water and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake for 12 minutes, until golden and bubbled. Cool, then snap into 12 shards.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 large shard. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Sesame Rice Flour Crackers
recipes.summary: Light gluten-free crackers made with rice and tapioca flour.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flours, sesame seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and boiling water until a dough forms.
Knead for 1 minute while warm, roll out between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2mm thick and cut into 24 squares.
Bake for 20 minutes, until pale golden and crisp. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackers. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container. Check the flour labels for gluten-free certification.

recipes.title: Nori Sesame Crisps
recipes.summary: Rice paper and nori baked into airy, salty crisps.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the sesame oil and tamari.
Dip each rice paper sheet in water for 3 seconds, lay on the tray, brush with the tamari oil, top with a piece of nori and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Cut into 4 with scissors.
Bake in batches for 8 minutes, until crisp and lightly golden. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Per serving: about 6 crisps. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Homemade Almond Butter
recipes.summary: Smooth roasted almond butter made with nothing but almonds and a pinch of salt.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roast the almonds on a tray for 12 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker.
Cool for 10 minutes, then blend in a food processor for 10 to 15 minutes, scraping down the sides, until the almonds turn from crumbs to a thick paste and then pour smooth.
Blend in the salt and oil, then spoon into a clean jar.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge; oil separation is normal, so stir. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Homemade Cashew Butter
recipes.summary: Mild, creamy cashew butter, lightly toasted for depth.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Toast the cashews on a tray for 10 minutes, until pale golden.
Cool for 10 minutes, then blend in a food processor for 10 to 12 minutes, scraping down often, until completely smooth and runny.
Blend in the salt and honey and spoon into a clean jar.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge. Contains tree nuts. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Homemade Sunflower Seed Butter
recipes.summary: A nut-free spread with a toasty flavour, made from roasted sunflower seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roast the seeds on a tray for 10 minutes, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Cool for 10 minutes, then blend in a food processor for 10 minutes, scraping down often, until thick and smooth.
Blend in the salt and oil, adding another spoonful of oil if it is too stiff, then spoon into a clean jar.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge. A nut-free option for lunchboxes, though check school rules on seeds.

recipes.title: Tahini Honey Halva Bites
recipes.summary: No-bake sesame bites with pistachios, firm enough to slice.
steps: Line a small loaf tin with baking paper. Warm the honey in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes until runny.
Stir the honey, vanilla and salt into the tahini until smooth, then fold in the pistachios.
Press into the tin and chill until firm. Lift out and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge. Contains sesame and tree nuts. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Hazelnut Chocolate Spread
recipes.summary: Silky roasted hazelnut and dark chocolate spread with no palm oil.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Toast the hazelnuts on a tray for 10 minutes, then rub in a tea towel to remove most of the skins.
Blend the nuts in a food processor for 8 minutes, scraping down often, until a smooth runny paste forms.
Melt the chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water for 4 minutes, until smooth. Blend it into the nut paste with the cocoa, icing sugar, oil and salt.
Spoon into a clean jar and cool.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 3 weeks in a cool cupboard or 2 months in the fridge. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Crunchy Roasted Peanut Spread
recipes.summary: Chunky peanut spread made with roasted peanuts, a touch of honey and salt.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Warm the peanuts on a tray for 10 minutes, until fragrant.
Blend 100g of the peanuts for 30 seconds, until just chopped, and set aside for crunch.
Blend the remaining peanuts with the honey and salt for 8 to 10 minutes, scraping down often, until smooth and glossy. Stir in the chopped peanuts and spoon into a jar.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge. Contains peanuts. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Eggless Spiced Apple Muffins
recipes.summary: Moist egg-free muffins with chunks of apple and a cinnamon sugar top.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, brown sugar and half the cinnamon. Whisk the soy milk, oil, vinegar and vanilla, pour into the dry mix and stir until just combined, then fold in the apple.
Divide among the cases, sprinkle with the raw sugar mixed with the remaining cinnamon and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Berry Muffins
recipes.summary: Tender gluten-free muffins dotted with frozen berries.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, baking powder and sugar. Whisk the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla, pour into the dry mix and stir until just combined, then fold in the berries.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 2 days at room temperature or 5 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months. Check the flour and baking powder labels for gluten-free certification.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.title: Vegan Chocolate Cupcakes
recipes.summary: Light, cocoa-rich cupcakes made without eggs or dairy.
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C fan (195°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Sift the flour, cocoa, sugar and bicarbonate of soda. Whisk the soy milk, oil, vinegar and vanilla, then stir into the dry mix until just smooth.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes, until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely and dust with icing sugar.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cupcake. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Mozzarella and Chive Scones
recipes.summary: Savoury gluten-free scones with melty mozzarella and fresh chives.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour and baking powder until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the mozzarella and chives.
Beat the egg with the milk, reserve a spoonful for glazing, and stir the rest into the dry mix to form a soft dough.
Pat out to 3cm thick, cut into 8 rounds, brush with the reserved egg mix and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 scone. Best on the day; keeps 2 days in the fridge and reheats at 160°C fan for 6 minutes. Check labels for gluten-free certification.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake the scones until cooked through.

recipes.title: Flourless Orange Almond Squares
recipes.summary: A moist gluten-free cake made with whole boiled oranges and almond meal.
steps: Cover the oranges with water in a saucepan and simmer for 45 minutes, until very soft. Drain, cool, halve, remove any pips and blend the whole fruit, skin and all, to a puree.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20 x 30cm tin. Whisk the eggs and sugar for 3 minutes until thick, then fold in the orange puree, almond meal and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Chewy Vegan Raisin Oat Rounds
recipes.summary: Chewy oat cookies with raisins and cinnamon, made without eggs or dairy.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, raisins, sugar, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda.
Stir in the oil and soy milk to form a firm dough, then roll into 12 balls and flatten to 1.5cm thick on the trays, 4cm apart.
Bake for 14 minutes, until golden at the edges but still soft in the centre. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cookie. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Fudge Brownies
recipes.summary: Dense, fudgy brownies made with almond meal instead of flour.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over barely simmering water for 5 minutes, until smooth, then cool slightly.
Whisk the sugar, eggs and vanilla for 3 minutes until thick and pale, stir in the chocolate mix, then fold in the almond meal, cocoa and salt.
Pour into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until the top is set and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months. Check the chocolate and cocoa labels for gluten. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until set and refrigerate within 2 hours in warm weather.

recipes.title: Vegan Carrot Cake Bites
recipes.summary: No-bake bliss balls with grated carrot, walnuts, sultanas and cinnamon.
steps: Blitz the oats and walnuts in a food processor for 30 seconds until coarsely ground.
Add the carrot, sultanas, maple syrup, 2 tbsp of the coconut and the cinnamon and blend for 1 minute, until the mixture sticks together when pinched.
Roll into 12 balls, then roll in the remaining coconut and chill until firm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bite. Keeps 5 days in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Lemon Polenta Squares
recipes.summary: Moist lemon cake squares made with polenta and almond meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Beat the butter, sugar and lemon zest for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the polenta, almond meal, baking powder and lemon juice, then spread into the tin.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate within 2 hours in warm weather.

recipes.title: Lemon Cashew Coconut Balls
recipes.summary: Vegan no-bake balls with raw cashews, lemon zest and coconut.
steps: Blitz the cashews and 70g of the coconut in a food processor for 1 minute, until finely ground.
Add the maple syrup, lemon zest, juice and salt and blend for 1 minute, until the mixture clumps together when pinched.
Roll into 12 balls, then roll in the remaining coconut and chill until firm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ball. Keeps 1 week in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer. Contains tree nuts.
